So long as there’s no unforeseen disaster that occurs at some point within the next few weeks, Grand Theft Auto VI should finally come out, and at the time of writing, it’s about a month away. A new Grand Theft Auto game is always a big deal, especially since Grand Theft Auto IV was a full-on gaming blockbuster in 2008, and then 2013’s Grand Theft Auto V was even bigger, and it impressively came out within the same console generation as IV.

So, the next generation would get a sixth Grand Theft Auto, right? Nope! The next generation got a remastered Grand Theft Auto V, with Grand Theft Auto Online making so much money that the sixth didn’t “have” to come out fast or anything. The wait has been 13 years now between games, but Grand Theft Auto VI is already a massive deal, and it will probably be the entertainment release of the year, which is impressive considering some of the blockbusters and acclaimed movies that have come out in 2026. Speaking of movies, these ones might well be good homework to watch before GTA 6, if you want a little indication of what the game might be like, or they're good to watch if you need something to fill the time while you anxiously await being able to play this long-awaited game (and especially if you’ve already played GTA 5 to death).

blocks.c: Gene Hackman, Warren Beatty, and Faye Dunaway robbing a bank as the characters in Bonnie and Clyde (1967)

blocks.x: The main way Grand Theft Auto VI is standing out narratively, compared to past games, is by having the two main characters be in a relationship as well as being partners in crime. It’s not the first GTA to let you play as more than one character, since GTA 5 had a trio of protagonists, but that personal connection between the two should make both gameplay and the narrative interesting for hopefully obvious reasons.

Bonnie and Clyde is a movie that has been brought up when discussing the narrative of GTA 6, as an influence, and it is pretty much the definitive movie about two people in love doing a bunch of crimes together. Maybe Badlands as well, but that’s a bit more of an arthouse thing, and also, Bonnie and Clyde is more focused on robberies and stuff, with the marketing and gameplay seen for GTA 6 so far emphasizing that kind of crime.

The title does let you know you're in for silliness, and the bromance angle comes about because Brian (returning from the first movie) and the newly introduced Roman do have some remarkable chemistry, and the pair get involved in a pretty wild series of events here.
The real reason 2 Fast 2 Furious is worth a shout-out here, though, is because it’s set in Miami, and that’s where GTA 6 is kinda/sorta set… at least the Grand Theft Auto world’s version of Miami.

Or technically, GTA 6 is set in a larger area than just Vice City: the state of Leonida, which is GTA’s Florida.

blocks.x: 2003 was a good year for over-the-top action/crime movies set in Miami, apparently, because Bad Boys II can be described that way, so it’s a very fitting double feature with 2 Fast 2 Furious. Miami is important to all four Bad Boys movies, sure, but Bad Boys II is probably the best of the bunch, and it’s also the wildest, which helps if you want a film that scratches the GTA itch.

There’s a ton of chaos, destruction, violence, and debauchery here, and while it’s not known exactly how wild Grand Theft Auto VI will be, it’ll probably feel at least a little zany in parts (and it’s unlikely to be as gritty and downbeat as Grand Theft Auto IV). The main characters of Bad Boys II sometimes act like they're the playable characters in a GTA or GTA-type game, and the version of Miami depicted here is also heightened in a way that'll likely be similar to Vice City being a more extravagant version of Miami in GTA 6.

blocks.x: Like Miami Vice (2006), Heat was directed by Michael Mann, and he’s a filmmaker who’s always understood how to best operate within the heist genre specifically, and maybe the crime and action genres more broadly. It’s kind of realistic in that way, and also very thought-provoking as to what it says about human nature and who people choose to idolize, even if they don’t realize they're doing that.
